_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), set 31/2/2 (Series A2DDC/2, booklet code 2131/2/2), sibling of 31/2/1. 24 page images (cover announces 23 printed pages; idx 23, folio 24, is BLANK apart from the footer, confirmed at full size). idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-22, Hindi on every odd index 1-21 (each the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked on the contact sheet, all Hindi, and every English page ends on a whole question or a whole alternative, so the parity holds throughout. Instructions confirm sci80: 39 questions, A Q1-20 MCQ x1, B Q21-26 x2, C Q27-33 x3, D Q34-36 x5, E Q37-39 case-based x4. Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (per-set file, footer 'X SCIENCE 31/2/2 PAGE n' on every page, header 'Paper Code: 31/2/2') for a bare OR: after Q21, 24, 27, 31, 35, 36, 37(c), 38(c), 39(c) = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. Q28, Q29, Q32 and Q34 print (a) and (b) with NO OR and one marks figure; the scheme awards both parts, so each is one row. No void notes anywhere in the scheme. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme as images; each was re-derived and all 20 agree. Sibling method: 38 rows are the same questions as 31/2/1 (confirmed on this paper's own pages) and copy the reference's stem/context/options/answer/chapter/subtopic/difficulty byte for byte; 16 rows are new and transcribed fresh. Two typesetting differences were NOT treated as new questions: Q10 prints 'true' without the underline that 31/2/1 Q8 carries (reference text kept so the row dedups), and Q13's bold-underlined DOES NOT matches 31/2/1 Q16, which the reference renders as bold. Decimal points on this paper are ORDINARY full stops (2.3 cm, 5.1, 1.5) although its marking scheme prints a raised dot (1·5); the paper wins.

questions.context: When electric current flows in a purely resistive circuit electrical energy gets fully converted into heat energy. The amount of heat produced (H) in the circuit is found to be directly proportional to (i) the square of current \((I^2)\) (ii) the resistance (R) of the conductor and (iii) the time (t) for which current flows. In other words \(H = I^2Rt\). Electrical devices such an electric fuse, electric heater, electric iron etc. are all based on this effect called heating effect of electric current.
